answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to post a bond before it can influence a shared decision, then slash that bond when its signed actions violate an auditable rule, such as submitting conflicting votes. A trellis of attestations can link votes to the same scarce, costly credential without claiming that names prove personhood; sable accounts do not gain weight merely by multiplying. The attacker must lock real capital in every identity and risks losing it, so scaling a Sybil campaign becomes expensive rather than free. A ferrous audit trail makes the penalties verifiable.
